item.description:

If you haven’t experienced Jazz Brunch yet, here’s what you can expect: from the moment the music begins, the taproom fills with that perfect weekend energy… laid-back jazz, fresh brunch plates, great beer, and a room full of people settling in and staying awhile. Friends gather around tables, conversations flow easily, and the rhythm of the music sets the tone for a perfect, easy Saturday. It’s exactly the kind of atmosphere we hoped to create when this idea first came to life!
We’re especially excited to continue working with our house Jazz band, “Four Peanuts”, whose smooth, soulful sound brings everything together. item.title: Graybeard Falls -- 6 mi, 1,200 ft. gain — Fri Nov 6, 8:45 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **PLEASE READ ENTIRE DESCRIPTION BELOW**
**Sign-up opens Sunday, Nov. 1st at 8 PM**
The Mt. Graybeard Trail is a favorite of many, myself included. We’ll do an out-and-back, around 3 miles up and the same coming back. There's a clearing by Graybeard Falls where we'll take a short break before heading down.
Because of a sustained uphill segment and lots of heads-down walking over roots & rocks, this hike earns a solid 5.0 difficulty level on a 10-point scale. If you ever use hiking poles, they'd be useful here. Parts of the uphill are definitely not in the "easy" category, so if you're a less experienced hiker and unsure whether you're okay with 1,000'+ in elevation gain, it's best to sit this one out rather than risk holding back the group. We'll move at a fairly good pace, averaging around 2.2 mph.
There are three stream crossings. One via a relatively new bridge, and the other two require some rock-hopping. The trail can be muddy in parts, too, so wear

item.title: 🌟 A Course in Miracles Study Group — Fri Nov 6, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Center for Spiritual Living Asheville **A Course In Miracles Study Group**
*✨ All are welcome to join us for A Course in Miracles at the Center for Spiritual Living Asheville!*
📅 When: First & Third Fridays of each month 🕐 Time: 1:00 PM – 2:30 PM 💜 Love Offering to support the Community
**🌟 About Our Gatherings** 🃏 During each meeting, we each choose a card from the "Miracle Cards" — inviting Spirit to guide us to exactly the right message for ourselves or the group in that moment. 📖 When time allows, we also share a lesson from the Workbook together. 🚪 You are welcome to join at any time — no need to start from the beginning!
**💡 New to ACIM? Here's the heart of it:** A miracle is a shift in perception from fear to Love. "Nothing real can be threatened, nothing unreal exists — therein lies the peace of God."
☮️ Come join us for some POG (Peace of God)!
🙏 Wishing you a year filled with Miracles, Love & Light!
With love, Marla (Facilitator) & Robin (Co-Facilitator)

item.title: Adult Studio: English Paper Piecing — Sat Dec 5, 1:00 PM
item.description:
No sewing machine, no problem. Long before home machines were prevalent, this straightforward hand sewing method uses two simple stitches to utilize precious fabric scraps into hexagonal quilt tops. In this three hour workshop, you will learn the techniques and methods brought over from early English settlers that are still used today. All materials provided. Jessica Kaufman earned her Masters degree in Craft Education, and teaches a wide variety of workshops in fibers and textiles, focusing mainly on dyeing, surface design, sewing, and knitting. Her studio in Asheville is open to the public for classes and custom orders. Find info at www.waxonstudio.com. REGISTER HERE

item.title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND — Sat Dec 19, 4:00 PM
item.description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.
Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.
The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.
Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by Uncle Paul (@unclepaul.music)
